# SOOS — Kernel Identity and Attestation (KIA)
# draft-sato-soos-kia-03
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/kia/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 4 July 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

KIA (Kernel Identity and Attestation) addresses the GEC spoofing problem: without attestation, a malicious process can impersonate a governance controller, sign fake audit records, and present false compliance evidence while the agent operates ungoverned. KIA defines the GEC keypair (or FROST threshold keypair in HA deployments), a three-level attestation hierarchy (L1 software / L2 sidecar / L3 TEE/hardware), and the GEC Manifest that binds the GEC's identity to its configuration at initialization. Version -03 adds FROST threshold signing for HA deployments, the XPID (Cross-Principal Identifier) for cross-instance federation audit correlation, and four new security considerations (CVE-2025-13609 class defense, CVE-2026-33697 class defense, FROST nonce reuse, XPID revocation gap). This document is the reference specification for the KIA RATS WG presentation at IETF 126 Vienna.

KIA is NOT: an agent identity protocol (that is WIMSE/SPIFFE), a policy enforcement protocol (that is CAP/Cedar), or an audit record format (that is GAR). KIA is the signing and attestation foundation that all others depend on.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without KIA, your SOOS-governed system has no standardized way to:

- Prove that the governance controller signing your audit records is the actual GEC running the defined Cedar policies, not a shadow process producing compliant-looking records while the agent operates freely
- Survive individual signing node failures without degrading to single-signer mode (FROST HA option, Section 4.1)
- Correlate an agent's governance trail across multiple GEC instances in a federation without a trusted third party (XPID, Section 6)
- Structurally prevent the CVE-2025-13609 class of identity takeover (Section 15.10) — where an attacker claims an existing agent UUID via duplicate registration
- Structurally prevent the CVE-2026-33697 class of attestation relay (Section 15.11) — where attestation evidence bound to a transport key is relayed to divert an attested session

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

These terms are normative in KIA-03 and must not be paraphrased away:

GEC Keypair / Threshold Keypair:  [UPDATED in -03]
   Standard deployments: Ed25519 keypair generated at deployment initialization and held in a hardware secure element. The private key MUST NOT be exported under any circumstances.
   FROST deployments: the GEC signing key is held as t-of-n secret shares across a signing cluster. No single node holds the full private key. The corresponding public key is a single Ed25519-compatible point. All KIA signing requirements apply to the threshold keypair.

FROST (Flexible Round-Optimized Schnorr Threshold Signatures):  [NEW in -03]
   Normative option for HA GEC deployments (Section 4.1). Key requirements: (a) each signing participant MUST generate a fresh nonce per signing operation — nonce reuse exposes secret shares (CONF-KIA-16, CONF-KIA-17); (b) quorum failure MUST result in signing refusal and KERNEL_AUDIT_ANOMALY, never degradation to single-signer (CONF-KIA-18, CONF-KIA-19); (c) threshold t MUST NOT be reduced without a new key generation ceremony (CONF-KIA-20). Deployment declaration: deployment_constraints[] entry "frost:t-of-n:<t>-<n>".

XPID (Cross-Principal Identifier):  [NEW in -03]
   A UUID-v5 value derived deterministically from the GEC's threshold public key fingerprint and the agent's Party Registry entry hash. Derivation: XPID = UUID5("6ba7b814-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8", kernel_keypair_fingerprint + ":" + party_registry_entry_hash). Properties: deterministic (any GEC with inputs can compute it), stable (within keypair+Party Registry entry lifetime), immutable, non-forgeable without key material. Recorded as soos.governance.xpid in every GAR governance span. MUST NOT be accepted as client-supplied value (CONF-KIA-21). CONF-KIA-22: MUST be recorded in every GAR audit entry. CONF-KIA-23: federated kernels MUST validate mandate jti against local Revocation Registry independently of XPID.

OQ-S-XPID-REV (XPID Revocation Gap):  [NEW in -03]
   Known open issue: mandate revocation adds the jti to the Revocation Registry but does not invalidate the XPID. A revoked agent's XPID remains computable. Mitigations: (a) always check jti against Revocation Registry before accepting cross-instance events (CONF-KIA-23); (b) subscribe to CAEP revocation stream (Section 6.5); (c) enforce GEC Manifest staleness limits. Resolution deferred to KIA-04.

xpid_derivation_version:  [NEW in -03]
   New GEC Manifest field. String (semver). Declares which XPID derivation algorithm this GEC instance implements. REQUIRED. Current normative value: "1.0". GECs that do not implement XPID MUST set this to "none".

GEC Manifest / Kernel Manifest:
   (Carried forward from KIA-02 — see prior llms.txt. The manifest_signature now covers xpid_derivation_version.)

Three-level attestation hierarchy (L1 / L2 / L3):
   (Carried forward from KIA-02 unchanged.)

INV-9 (Event Log signing), INV-10 (Policy Change Attestation), INV-11 (Revocation Registry):
   (Carried forward from KIA-02 unchanged.)

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

RATS (RFC 9334):
   KIA-03 presents two novel RATS contributions at Vienna: (a) XPID as a cross-domain Attester identity correlation primitive — addresses the gap where RATS provides no mechanism for correlating Attester-signed artifacts across federation boundaries without a trusted third party; (b) CVE-2026-33697 defense as a concrete case study of how hardware-rooted attester identity prevents attestation relay attacks. The GEC Manifest remains RATS Evidence extended with SOOS governance-specific fields.

FROST (draft-irtf-cfrg-frost):
   KIA-03 profiles FROST for the GEC keypair case. The nonce generation requirements (Section 15.8), quorum failure behavior (CONF-KIA-18), and GEC Manifest declaration format are the KIA-specific profile constraints. The normative reference is Section 5 of [FROST] for nonce generation.

WIMSE:
   XPID addresses the WIMSE gap: no existing WIMSE specification provides cross-domain workload identity correlation without a shared identity provider. The XPID uses only KIA identity infrastructure already present in both kernels.

CAEP + SSF (RFC9672):
   Section 6.5 specifies the CAEP propagation model for XPID-bearing mandate revocation. mandate_revoked event type with subject format "xpid" requested for registration.

GAR-03 (draft-sato-soos-gar-03):
   XPID is recorded as soos.governance.xpid in every GAR governance span. XPID_DERIVED and XPID_VERIFICATION_FAILED ALE types requested for IANA registration.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft has no normative dependencies on other SOOS drafts (KIA is the trust anchor).

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — KIA-signed entries; XPID in soos.governance.xpid; XPID_DERIVED and XPID_VERIFICATION_FAILED ALE types
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-05) — HEM events KIA-signed; INV-HEM-01 L1/L2/L3 conformance levels reference KIA
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-04) — CAP Violation Records KIA-signed; BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE consent check uses MJWT aud-bound to kernel_keypair_fingerprint
   MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-02) — MJWT aud claim MUST equal kernel_keypair_fingerprint from GEC Manifest; Revocation Registry managed by KIA
   MAD (draft-sato-soos-mad-03) — cluster events KIA-signed; CAEP revocation stream sourced from MAD
   AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-02) — AEP session events KIA-signed
   SOV (draft-sato-soos-sov-02) — SO event stream entries KIA-signed
